## Bridger Aerospace Awarded 220-day Department of the Interior Task Order for 2027 with Multi-Mission King Air 350


October 15, 2026 8:00am EDT[Download as PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_475fd9b37e2e6b7e83ac4ff675c71924/bridgeraerospace/news/2026-10-15_Bridger_Aerospace_Awarded_220_day_Department_of_94.pdf)


### Exclusive-use task order with minimum guaranteed award of $5.3 million supports the U.S. Wildland Fire Service in 2027


BELGRADE, Mont., Oct. 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Bridger Aerospace Group Holdings, Inc. (“Bridger,” “Bridger Aerospace” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: BAER, BAERW), one of the nation’s leading aerial firefighting companies, today announced it has been awarded a 220-day task order by the U.S. Department of the Interior (the “DOI”) to provide 2027 air attack flight services in support of the U.S. Wildland Fire Service. The task order, issued under Bridger’s existing contract with the DOI, has a minimum guaranteed award value of approximately $5.3 million, subject to the terms of the task order.


Under the task order, Bridger will dedicate its King Air 350 aircraft for an exclusive-use period of 220 calendar days, which is currently anticipated to begin on or around March 1, 2027.


Following modifications at Bridger’s FAA-certified repair station, the aircraft was deployed by Bridger this summer under a 112-day task order. The aircraft is equipped with Blackhawk engine upgrades that deliver jet-like speed, superior loiter time, and outstanding low-altitude performance. It also features Garmin avionics, dual sensor systems, and real-time data dissemination capabilities, including Wide Area Motion Imagery (WAMI) technology paired with the proven MX-15 electro-optical/infrared (EO/IR) sensor.


“This award gives us the opportunity to put our people, aircraft, and intelligence capabilities to work for the Bureau of Indian Affairs across more of the 2027 wildfire season,” said Sam Davis, President and Chief Executive Officer of Bridger. “The King Air 350 will help deliver the information crews need from above to make decisions on the ground and act quickly when every second counts, which is at the heart of Bridger’s mission: helping protect lives, communities, and the land people depend on.”


The task order is scheduled to run through the 2027 wildfire season, with an exclusive-use period ending in early October 2027. The task order may be extended by mutual agreement of the parties.


**About Bridger Aerospace**


Based in Belgrade, Montana, Bridger Aerospace Group Holdings, Inc. is one of the nation’s largest aerial firefighting companies. Bridger provides aerial firefighting and wildfire management services to federal and state government agencies, including the United States Forest Service, across the nation, as well as internationally. More information about Bridger Aerospace is available at https://www.bridgeraerospace.com.
